summary.html: Agent reliability is becoming an engineering problem, not a prompting problem: the strongest AI posts were about verification loops, synthetic QA channels, and vendor constraints that push teams toward explicit tooling and billing.

Open models keep gaining practical momentum: Gemma 4 drew attention as both a teachable multimodal architecture and a deployable local model, while open-training efforts kept attracting serious talent.

The macro tape was dominated by Iran-war spillovers: the feed kept circling back to Hormuz, oil-sensitive inflation, and bond-market whipsaws as the real channels through which geopolitics can hit portfolios.

Outside pure finance, the useful signal came from physical systems and privacy: Japan is deploying robots into understaffed roles, Artemis II is nearing its lunar flyby, and browser fingerprinting stories are a reminder that mainstream platforms still collect more than most users assume.

items.title: @steipete: Anthropic Harness Access Tightens
items.body: Peter Steinberger flagged that Anthropic appears to be tightening access for first-party harness workflows, returning a billing-related error on a CLI harness call. The practical takeaway is to expect bring-your-own-credits economics and avoid depending on a single vendor path for agent tooling.

items.title: @steipete: Synthetic QA for Agents
items.body: This was one of the strongest workflow posts in the batch: use an orchestrator to assign real tasks, verify the result, and automatically spawn a fixer agent when checks fail. It points toward agent systems that look more like CI pipelines than chat sessions.

items.title: @_philschmid: Gemma 4 Visual Guide
items.body: Philipp Schmid recommended a diagram-heavy guide that explains Gemma 4's multimodal stack, MoE inference, and phone-friendly 2B deployment tricks. Useful because it translates open-model hype into concrete architectural ideas builders can actually reason about.

items.title: @TechCrunch: Copilot's Legal Warning Label
items.body: TechCrunch highlighted that Microsoft's own terms frame Copilot outputs as something users should not treat as authoritative. That is less a gotcha than a reminder that legal disclaimers are still lagging far behind the way people want to use AI at work.

items.title: @eliebakouch: Prime Intellect Adds Open-Training Talent
items.body: Elie Bakouch said he is joining Prime Intellect to work on pre- and mid-training for open models. The signal is that frontier-level talent is still flowing toward smaller open efforts that think focused teams can push training research forward.

items.title: @TheEconomist: Bond Markets in a Tug of War
items.body: The Economist framed sovereign debt markets as a tug-of-war between inflation risk and recession risk as the Iran war ripples outward. For investors, that means rate signals may stay noisy even when the geopolitical story feels directionally obvious.

items.title: @TheEconomist: Hormuz Is the Market Chokepoint
items.body: The sharp point here is not just military escalation, but the market plumbing: a Hormuz disruption would hit a meaningful chunk of global oil flow and keep energy prices elevated. The post also argued that reopening the strait would be operationally hard even for the U.S.

items.title: @TheEconomist: Inflation Is Becoming Political Again
items.body: The Economist tied Trump's approval weakness to inflation sensitivity, arguing that a costly war matters politically when voters are already primed to punish price pressure. It is a useful reminder that macro and politics are feeding each other, not moving independently.

items.title: @FactSet: S&P Valuation Still Not Cheap
items.body: FactSet's latest snapshot puts the S&P 500's forward P/E roughly in line with its 5-year average but still above its 10-year norm. In plain English, the market is no longer screamingly stretched, but it still is not cheap on a longer historical view.

items.title: @NASA: Artemis II Nears Lunar Flyby
items.body: NASA posted Orion's last look at Earth before Artemis II's closest lunar approach, a reminder that the mission is now in the operational phase rather than launch-pageantry mode. Beyond the visuals, it marks the most tangible step toward a sustained crewed return to the Moon in years.

items.title: @TechCrunch: Japan's Robots Fill Labor Gaps
items.body: TechCrunch's point was that Japan's robotics push is being driven less by sci-fi ambition than by labor shortages in jobs people do not want. That is a cleaner mental model for near-term physical AI adoption: fill gaps first, replace broad labor later.

items.title: @thenextweb: LinkedIn Fingerprinting Warning
items.body: TNW reported that LinkedIn runs a hidden script that probes thousands of Chrome extensions and collects device signals without clearly disclosing it in the privacy policy. If accurate, it is one more reason to treat mainstream web platforms as aggressive telemetry systems by default.
